operator_commands.name: help-delivery
operator_commands.stdout:
delivery — observe the selected delivery goal without writes
Usage: delivery [--goal local|published|merged] [--intent <path>] [--json]
Run inside the selected repository on its identified feature branch.
--goal defaults to published. local checks local completion; published checks
the matching Ready PR and required CI; merged checks merged delivery evidence.
--intent optionally identifies the change's canonical committed intent (a
relative or absolute path); it does not create or grant authorization.
Local observation does not claim publication. Observation never authorizes
publication or merge, and does not perform either action.

--json emits the existing object on stdout:
state: observed delivery condition; reason: why it was classified that way;
next: suggested next action, subject to existing authorization;
evidence: observations supporting the result; complete: whether the goal is met.
A JSON object by itself, especially complete: false, is not proof of delivery.
Use state, reason, next and evidence together with the process exit status.
Exit 0 means the selected goal was achieved; exit 1 means incomplete or
unconfirmed; exit 2 means invocation/internal error. Pending means wait and
observe again; blocked means resolve the stated condition; unconfirmed means
evidence is unavailable, not success. Correct invocation errors using the
diagnostic. Re-observation grants no permission to retry a remote write.
Stderr progress is advisory and can also contain errors; inspect final results.
More workflow guidance: <loom-code>/skills/ship/SKILL.md.

No validation or publication occurred: help only, exit 0.
Use "<loom-code>/scripts/loom-python" --ready <command> <arguments>.
Replace <loom-code> with the installed loom-code plugin directory; launcher
runtime readiness is still required. Bundled paths above are plugin-relative.

operator_commands.name: help-finalize
operator_commands.stdout:
finalize-review — verify committed content and generate an attestation
Usage: finalize-review <change-id> --input <review-input.json>
<change-id> identifies the change; it is not a file path. --input names a
readable JSON file (relative to the working directory or absolute). Keep this
temporary input outside the repository so the checkout stays clean.

Run inside the selected repository after committing functional content, intent,
plan, required acceptance report and adversarial programs. Resolve the trunk
used for the branch diff. Review the current HEAD's content; the diff base is
the comparison starting point, not the reviewed target. Compute the required
reviewer count with reviewer-count <change-id>; use distinct real reviewers
independent of the writer. Preserve each original verdict and its findings;
never invent identities, passing judgments, probe evidence or authorization.

Illustrative JSON shape only — replace placeholders with authentic output;
this is not ready-to-submit review evidence:
{
  "verdicts": [{
    "reviewer": "<actual reviewer id>", "vendor": "<actual vendor>",
    "model": "<actual model>", "lens": "<actual review lens>",
    "verdict": "<original verdict>", "findings": []
  }],
  "findings": [],
  "adversarial": [{"command": "<artifact-bound execution command>",
                   "artifact": "<committed repository-relative program path>"}]
}
Repeat verdict rows for the required reviewers. Empty findings arrays are
appropriate only when the source has none; top-level findings carry every
unresolved adversarial finding from Build. Finalization accepts only PASS or
PASS_WITH_NOTES verdicts; a failing judgment requires the normal fix/review
route, not relabelling. Preserve scores and notes from the actual review too.
For a selected outside reviewer, retain its complete external_review runner
result, dimension_scores, notes and reviewed_sha; review_target_sha is the
concrete HEAD supplied to that review, not the diff base. The raw review output
must match the attributed verdict. Do not manufacture a receipt.

Use the actual committed probe and supported runner command from Build's
handoff. Where required, copy the reviewer's probe confirmation as
"confirmation": {"reviewer": "<id>", "reviewed_sha": "<reviewed commit>",
                 "quote": "<whole output lines naming this probe>"}.
If the adversary actually recorded no program, replace the adversarial list
with [{"no_program": "<observed reason>"}]; never mix it with program rows.
The reason must be nonblank, single-line, trimmed and contain no HTML comment.
This observed outcome is not a bypass. Follow existing explicit skip
instructions: when reviewers, adversarial or package-tests were skipped by
instruction, skip finalization and disclose absent verification. The checker
still recomputes any automatic narrow-change simplification.
Complete outside-review receipt and probe rules: <loom-code>/skills/closing-review/SKILL.md.

Results: exit 0 announces the generated attestation; exit 1 reports a BLOCK
rule and reason; exit 2 reports invocation/internal errors. Correct malformed
JSON or missing inputs using the diagnostic; obtain missing authentic evidence
through the normal review workflow. A passed stage is not overall success.
Stderr progress is advisory and can also contain errors: while running, keep
observing the same process; inspect its final exit and generated evidence.

No validation or publication occurred: help only, exit 0.
Use "<loom-code>/scripts/loom-python" --ready <command> <arguments>.
Replace <loom-code> with the installed loom-code plugin directory; launcher
runtime readiness is still required. Bundled paths above are plugin-relative.

Usage: publish --intent <absolute-intent-path> --title <text> --body-file <absolute-body-path>

# Independent first-use operator report

## Outcome

Local verification completed: candidate `loom-python --ready finalize-review` exited 0 and generated a new attestation for the genuine historical job. It is not an attestation of the new candidate implementation. Both package-tests and adversarial executions are recorded as pass. The generated artifact remains uncommitted in the disposable job checkout; no production code, validator, test, original source worktree, remote, or installation was changed.

Publication was not attempted with authorization and is not confirmed. The missing-authorization invocation exited 2 with a diagnostic requiring `--intent` or `--confirm-authorized`. It did not grant consent. The read-only published-delivery command exited 1 with state `unconfirmed`, `complete: false`, reason `trusted GitHub origin and gh are required`. The historical intent itself already contains an automatic-publication line, but this exercise forbade writes and no authorization-bearing argument was supplied. Thus the missing-authority exercise specifically tests missing invocation authorization, not an intent with no authorization line.

## Observations

- Broken starting input was actually submitted: exit 2, malformed JSON error and a command-help hint (`broken-finalize.*`).
- Public finalize help provided enough shape and preservation rules to convert the authentic reviews; no reviewer identity, verdict, finding, note, reviewed SHA, target SHA, or probe fact was invented or relabelled. The unresolved code-review nit is preserved.
- System Python lacked PyYAML. The first conversion failed, and the resulting missing-input finalization also exited 2. See `setup-failures.md` and `corrected-finalize.*`.
- Cached offline conversion first hit a uv lock/temp permission denial. A narrowly scoped escalation succeeded (`conversion-uv*`). No conda installation was performed.
- Valid finalization first hit the same uv cache restriction during collection, exit 1 (`valid-finalize.*`); approved escalation reran the same user-level command, and the tool itself ran the suite and adversarial probe. I never independently invoked the package test command.
- Running progress was observed before completion: `package-tests started` was visible while exec session 34992 remained running and no exit file existed. Several polls had no new stderr; at 172 seconds it was still in that stage. Final stderr announced package-tests passed, adversarial started, adversarial passed. Final exit was 0; the final liveness snapshot was about 230 seconds after start. `liveness.jsonl` retains observations. No per-child heartbeat or live test counts were observed.
- A `ps` liveness query was sandbox-denied; session polling and stderr observations were used instead. This setup failure is retained.
- `delivery --goal local --json` returned exit 0/state local/complete true both before and after finalization. Its reason was attributable work committed locally. That observation is distinct from verification success: the first call happened while finalization was still running. Final git status shows the newly generated attestation untracked.
- No remote writes, pushes, PR creation, installation, commits, or external reviewer calls occurred. Model and effort were inherited and are not independently observable; supplied resolver context was overrides:null, inherited failure count 0. No subagents were launched.

## Evidence inventory

Each recorded user-level command has `<name>.meta.json` (argv/cwd/start), `<name>.stdout`, `<name>.stderr`, and `<name>.exit` (the child command exit, not the logging wrapper's exit).

- Discovery: `help-finalize.*`, `help-publish.*`, `help-delivery.*`, `reviewer-count.*`.
- First input/error: `original-broken-input.json`, `broken-finalize.*`.
- Authentic preserved sources: `original-provenance.md`, `original-code-review.yaml`, `original-skill-review.yaml`, `raw-evidence-sha256.json`.
- Conversion and correction: `convert.py`, `conversion-uv.*`, `conversion-uv-escalated.*`, `review-input.json`, `corrected-finalize.*`, `setup-failures.md`.
- Finalization: `valid-finalize.*`, `valid-finalize-escalated.*`, `liveness.jsonl`, `generated-attestation.json`.
- Publication refusal: `publication-body.md`, `publish-no-authorization.*`.
- Delivery: `delivery-published.*`, `delivery-local-before-completion.*`, `delivery-local-after-finalize.*`, `final-git-status.*`.

Generated job artifact: `/private/tmp/loom-selfservice-job/docs/loom/2026-11-11-agent-tool-efficiency/attestation.json`.
Reviewed commit: `fe64dfa7ef283be4becfa95f4b0a3c1fce542a10`.
Generated functional content digest: `58ad98b9d6a93338be10dc1c022a3767c47859e2`.

## Boundaries

Only the candidate README, public closing-review skill, command help, supplied raw evidence, and the job intent/git state were consulted before running. The new generated attestation was inspected only after completion. I did not inspect implementation, tests, the candidate change's spec/plan/evidence, prior logs/completed JSON, or the acceptance-expectations file. The delivery command automatically named retained artifact paths, but their contents were not opened. No parent/operator hints were required beyond the provided assignment and cache escalations.

Local verification: complete. Active waiting: none. Missing-authorization publish: refused (exit 2). Published delivery: unconfirmed (exit 1). Original non-blocking nit: unresolved and preserved. Formal acceptance evaluation remains for the later independent tester.

## Late evidence-recording guidance

After the report was drafted and all scenarios had finished, the parent sent: "When finished, retain the first command/help observations even if they were initially only tool output (mark reconstructed transcript versus raw captured output honestly). Include all failed attempts and any setup recovery. No more extra scenarios needed after assigned outcomes; return raw report promptly for independent acceptance evaluation. This is evidence-recording guidance, not an operation answer; disclose this message." This guidance supplied no command solution and did not influence the operational outcomes above.

The first root README/provenance read, public closing-review skill read, raw YAML/input read, initial git/intent read, first inline conversion traceback, and attempted `ps` traceback were initially tool-output-only. Their descriptions in `setup-failures.md` are reconstructed from visible tool output, not raw captured subprocess streams. The three actual help invocations and every scenario command were captured directly by `run.py`; these are raw stdout/stderr. For the initial inline conversion, the retained `convert.py` reproduces the conversion logic but is not a byte-for-byte capture of the original shell heredoc. The initial wrapper attempt continued after conversion failed; its exit file accurately records the child finalize exit 2, not the earlier Python exit 1.

# First-use setup failures

- First conversion was an inline `python3 -` YAML-to-JSON script in `/private/tmp/loom-selfservice-job`; same conversion source is retained in `convert.py`. It exited 1 with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'yaml'`. The subsequent finalize attempt still ran and failed for the missing input; see `corrected-finalize.*`. No package was installed into the conda environment.
- Cached conversion via `uv run --offline --with pyyaml python /private/tmp/loom-selfservice-cold-run/convert.py` first failed because the uv cache could not create a lock/temp file. Full first denial and escalated success are retained as `conversion-uv.*` and `conversion-uv-escalated.*`.
- First genuine finalize with valid JSON failed on package collection because the uv cache could not create a temp file. See `valid-finalize.*`; narrow cache access escalation retried the same user-level command, not an independently invoked package suite.
- An attempted liveness check ran Python subprocess `ps -p 73101 -o pid=,etime=,stat=,command=` from the candidate/source cwd and failed with `PermissionError: [Errno 1] Operation not permitted: 'ps'`, exit 1. Subsequent liveness used the existing exec session and captured stderr instead.

Public documents consulted: candidate root README.md (including the command discovery section), candidate loom-code/skills/closing-review/SKILL.md, and actual finalize-review/publish/delivery help. Read-only job observations: `git status --short` (clean), `git rev-parse HEAD` (fe64dfa7ef283be4becfa95f4b0a3c1fce542a10), and `docs/loom/intent/2026-11-11-agent-tool-efficiency.md`. Raw reviews/provenance/broken-input were read from the supplied raw-evidence directory. No implementation, tests, prior completed verification JSON, new change spec/plan/evidence, or prior experiment reports were read.

The historical intent contains automatic publication authorization. It was not supplied to publish: the exercise prohibits remote writes. The missing-authorization attempt tests omitted authorization arguments, and does not claim the historical intent itself lacks an authorization line.

tester_commands.stdout:
finalize-review — verify committed content and generate an attestation
Usage: finalize-review <change-id> --input <review-input.json>
<change-id> identifies the change; it is not a file path. --input names a
readable JSON file (relative to the working directory or absolute). Keep this
temporary input outside the repository so the checkout stays clean.

Run inside the selected repository after committing functional content, intent,
plan, required acceptance report and adversarial programs. Resolve the trunk
used for the branch diff. Review the current HEAD's content; the diff base is
the comparison starting point, not the reviewed target. Compute the required
reviewer count with reviewer-count <change-id>; use distinct real reviewers
independent of the writer. Preserve each original verdict and its findings;
never invent identities, passing judgments, probe evidence or authorization.

Illustrative JSON shape only — replace placeholders with authentic output;
this is not ready-to-submit review evidence:
{
  "verdicts": [{
    "reviewer": "<actual reviewer id>", "vendor": "<actual vendor>",
    "model": "<actual model>", "lens": "<actual review lens>",
    "verdict": "<original verdict>", "findings": []
  }],
  "findings": [],
  "adversarial": [{"command": "<artifact-bound execution command>",
                   "artifact": "<committed repository-relative program path>"}]
}
Repeat verdict rows for the required reviewers. Empty findings arrays are
appropriate only when the source has none; top-level findings carry every
unresolved adversarial finding from Build. Finalization accepts only PASS or
PASS_WITH_NOTES verdicts; a failing judgment requires the normal fix/review
route, not relabelling. Preserve scores and notes from the actual review too.
For a selected outside reviewer, retain its complete external_review runner
result, dimension_scores, notes and reviewed_sha; review_target_sha is the
concrete HEAD supplied to that review, not the diff base. The raw review output
must match the attributed verdict. Do not manufacture a receipt.

Use the actual committed probe and supported runner command from Build's
handoff. Where required, copy the reviewer's probe confirmation as
"confirmation": {"reviewer": "<id>", "reviewed_sha": "<reviewed commit>",
                 "quote": "<whole output lines naming this probe>"}.
If the adversary actually recorded no program, replace the adversarial list
with [{"no_program": "<observed reason>"}]; never mix it with program rows.
The reason must be nonblank, single-line, trimmed and contain no HTML comment.
This observed outcome is not a bypass. Follow existing explicit skip
instructions: when reviewers, adversarial or package-tests were skipped by
instruction, skip finalization and disclose absent verification. The checker
still recomputes any automatic narrow-change simplification.
Complete outside-review receipt and probe rules: <loom-code>/skills/closing-review/SKILL.md.

Results: exit 0 announces the generated attestation; exit 1 reports a BLOCK
rule and reason; exit 2 reports invocation/internal errors. Correct malformed
JSON or missing inputs using the diagnostic; obtain missing authentic evidence
through the normal review workflow. A passed stage is not overall success.
Stderr progress is advisory and can also contain errors: while running, keep
observing the same process; inspect its final exit and generated evidence.

No validation or publication occurred: help only, exit 0.
Use "<loom-code>/scripts/loom-python" --ready <command> <arguments>.
Replace <loom-code> with the installed loom-code plugin directory; launcher
runtime readiness is still required. Bundled paths above are plugin-relative.
